audience: Local Wisent operators, coding-agent integrators, security and release operators, and incident responders who need one policy-preserving catalogue of approved agent-tool surfaces.
problem: Registering many MCP servers independently creates naming collisions and inconsistent launch and security configuration, while blindly aggregating child tools can turn binary or schema drift into an authority escalation.
promise: One local, policy-preserving MCP federation layer for an operator-approved catalogue of Wisent agent tools.

secondaryAction.label: Inspect the registry
secondaryAction.purpose: Review the static surfaces, signed release checks, and namespaced tools.

approvedClaims.claim: Las is a local catalogue and policy-preserving federation layer for Wisent agent tools.
approvedClaims.evidence: README.md#Las: Every Tool Your AI Agents Need Through One MCP

approvedClaims.claim: Las discovers an operator-approved set of sibling MCP servers, verifies signed release contracts, and exposes them through one stdio MCP server and one read-only CLI.
approvedClaims.evidence: README.md#Las: Every Tool Your AI Agents Need Through One MCP

approvedClaims.claim: Las provides deterministic surface__tool namespacing and launches children from a static repository-owned registry.
Signed release manifests bind child command, working directory, arguments, environment names, binary and code digests, tool names, and input-schema digests.
Las never inherits the complete parent environment and rejects ordinary surface environment names that look like raw secrets.
Las does not broaden child permissions, implement child behavior, install or repair products, or act as a raw secret broker.
approvedClaims.evidence: README.md#Las: Every Tool Your AI Agents Need Through One MCP; README.md#Explicit non-goals and limitations

approvedClaims.claim: A missing, invalid, expired, rolled-back, or byte-and-schema-mismatched release fails closed for that surface while remaining surfaces can still federate.
Las list reads registry and configuration state without spawning children, while las check initializes selected children and verifies their advertised tools without invoking a child tool.
Las opens no sockets; it communicates with its client and spawned children only through stdio.
The current public development source requires Node.js 18 or newer, a coordinated local Wisent workspace, and operator-provisioned signed release files.
approvedClaims.evidence: README.md#Las: Every Tool Your AI Agents Need Through One MCP; README.md#Quick start

requiredProof: The exact signed manifest bindings and sequence watermark boundary.
The las list, las tools, las check, and las-mcp source interfaces.
The fail-closed per-surface behavior and explicit non-goals.

rules: Use the canonical Wisent type, color, spacing, radius, and motion tokens.
Make the federation, signed-release, child-authority, and stdio boundaries concrete.
Use one primary action and source-backed CLI or contract evidence.
forbidden: Calling Las hosted service discovery, a package installer, a sandbox, or a secret broker.
Claims that Las makes unavailable children healthy or proves child safety and correctness.
Stable package publication, hosted organization catalogue, managed installation, availability SLA, or complete MCP support claims.
Invented tool counts, uptime, performance, adoption, security guarantees, fake output, generic AI gradients, or glass cards.

notes: Preserve the current landing's connected-system positioning only as the source-backed policy-preserving local federation contract.
Child products remain responsible for their own authorization and behavior.
